content.text: {"persuasion":"PERSUADED","support_scope":"FULL","rationale":"The book's core claim is that 'works of the law' has no single fixed deed-class as its referent; the surrounding context identifies the deeds (God's own law in Rom 3:20 and Gal 3:10, a circumcision-party demand in Gal 2:11-16, unnamed acts in Gal 3:2, 5), while the constant element is the denied claim — that such deeds can purchase justification, produce the Spirit, or place God in debt. This reading absorbs the evidence of both major rivals. The traditional Protestant reading correctly sees Torah in Rom 3:20 and Gal 3:10 but strains when it extends the phrase into a symbol of legalism opposed to law-keeping itself, because Paul immediately says faith establishes the law (Rom 3:31), calls the law holy, just, good, and spiritual (Rom 7:12, 14, 22), and pairs 'not of works' with commanded good works (Eph 2:9-10; Titus 3:5, 8). The New Perspective correctly explains the Antioch table-fellowship setting of Gal 2:16 and the circumcision flashpoint, but cannot explain Gal 3:10, where Paul defines the phrase's field by quoting Deut 27:26 — the curse for failing to do 'all things written in the book of the law' — or Rom 3:20, where the law in view gives knowledge of sin, functions no ethnic badge performs. The book's contextual-referent-plus-constant-denial model explains every occurrence without forcing either text, handles the Rom 9:32 textual variant transparently, and accounts for counter-evidence (1 Cor 7:19; Acts 15-16; Luke 17:10; Rom 4:4) that both rivals leave in tension. No supplied counter-reading explains a text the book cannot; therefore the book wins the comparative inference, including its printed elaborations, which the proving chapter substantiates verse by verse.","book_core_identification":"'Works of the law' is Paul's phrase for deeds considered in relation to law, with no single unchanging referent: the surrounding context identifies which deeds are in view (God's law, a circumcision-party demand, or unnamed acts), while the uniform and defining element is the rejected claim made for those deeds — that they can purchase justification, produce the Spirit, establish covenant standing, or place God in debt.","book_secondary_elaborations":["The phrase is not a synonym for obedience; a work names a deed, obedience names its relation to a legitimate command, and the two meet without becoming synonyms (Luke 17:10; Heb 11:8; Jas 2:22).","The classification table assigning each occurrence: Rom 3:20, 28 and Gal 3:10 as God's law explicitly, Gal 2:16 as circumcision-party application, Gal 3:2, 5 as ambiguous unnamed acts.","The Rom 9:32 textual note: KJV/TR reads 'works of the law' while the critical text reads 'as it were by works,' shifting weight to the attempted manner rather than a different code.","The broader companion argument that telos in Rom 10:4 means goal rather than termination, and that Paul's various named laws (law of God, law of sin, law of faith, law of Christ) must not be poured into one bucket.","The economic framing from Rom 4:4 — the excluded work is defined by its wage-claim, making the payer a debtor — as the mechanism uniting all occurrences."],"strongest_counter_interpretation":"The New Perspective reading (Sanders, Dunn, Wright): 'works of the law' refers throughout to one recognizable class of deeds — the Jewish covenant boundary markers of circumcision, food laws, and calendar/Sabbath observance — and Paul's polemic targets ethnic exclusivism, the requirement that Gentiles adopt Jewish identity markers, not human effort or the law generally. Its evidence is strong where the phrase first appears: Gal 2:11-16 sits inside the Antioch table-fellowship dispute with 'them which were of the circumcision'; circumcision is the letter's flashpoint (Gal 5:2-6; 6:12-15); Rom 3:29-30 follows Rom 3:28 with 'Is he the God of the Jews only?'; and 4QMMT supplies a Second Temple parallel where the phrase names specific halakhic observances.","counter_core_identification":"'Works of the law' denotes a fixed, specific class of deeds — Jewish identity and boundary practices (circumcision, food laws, Sabbath/calendar) — and Paul's denial targets ethnic exclusivism and covenant-membership badges rather than deeds-in-relation-to-law generally or a merit claim as such.","counter_relation_to_book_core":"CONTRADICTS","material_core_denial":"The counter denies the book's claim that the phrase has no unchanging referent and that context alone identifies the deeds; it asserts instead that one stable class of deeds (boundary markers) is the referent in every occurrence, so that Rom 3:20 and Gal 3:10 must also be read as targeting Jewish identity badges rather than God's law as a whole.","counter_case":["Gal 2:16 first occurs in the Antioch dispute over table fellowship, where Peter 'fearing them which were of the circumcision' withdrew from Gentiles (Gal 2:11-14) — the live issue is Jewish separation practice, not merit theology.","Circumcision is the concrete controversy of Galatians (Gal 5:2-6; 6:12-15) and of the Jerusalem council (Acts 15:1), suggesting the phrase names that controversy's deeds.","Rom 3:28 flows directly into 'Is he the God of the Jews only?' (Rom 3:29-30), tying justification apart from works of the law to the inclusion of Gentiles.","4QMMT uses 'some of the works of the Torah' for specific sectarian observances, supplying a documented Second Temple usage of the phrase for a delimited set of practices.","On this reading Paul never attacks obedience or the law itself, which coheres with Rom 3:31 and Rom 7:12."],"book_explanatory_advantages":["Gal 3:10 defines the phrase's field by quoting Deut 27:26 — the curse on 'every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them' — which is the whole Torah, not a subset of boundary markers; the book classifies this occurrence as God's law explicitly and the counter cannot.","Rom 3:20 grounds the denial in 'by the law is the knowledge of sin,' a function of the moral content of God's law that ethnic badges do not perform; Rom 3:31 then establishes that same law, which the book's reading requires and predicts.","The book simultaneously explains the NPP's best evidence: it assigns Gal 2:16 to the circumcision-party application on the strength of Gal 2:12-14, so the Antioch context is accounted for rather than explained away.","The constant across all occurrences — justification (Rom 3:20, 28; Gal 2:16), the Spirit (Gal 3:2, 5), escape from the curse (Gal 3:10) — is a denied claim, not a deed-class, exactly as the entry states; the economic mechanism is textually anchored in Rom 4:4 ('the reward not reckoned of grace, but of debt') and Luke 17:10.","The book resolves the standing counter-evidence to the traditional symbolic extension: Eph 2:9-10 excludes works as purchase price then ordains them as fruit; Titus 3:5 with 3:8; 1 Cor 7:19 separates the boundary mark from keeping God's commandments; Acts 16:3 (Timothy's circumcision) shows the deed itself is not the evil.","It keeps the Rom 9:32 textual variant visible and shows both readings converge on the attempted manner ('as it were by works') rather than a hidden code, strengthening the constant-denial thesis."],"counter_explanatory_advantages":["The counter gives a cleaner single answer to why the phrase erupts precisely in circumcision controversies (Antioch, Galatia, Jerusalem) and why Rom 3:29-30 immediately raises the Jew-Gentile question.","4QMMT provides an extrabiblical attestation of the phrase used for a delimited set of observances, which the book's flexible-referent account does not need but also does not match as neatly.","It offers a simpler sociological account of Paul's opponents than a theology of merit-claims does."],"evidence_book_core_cannot_explain":[],"comparative_winner":"BOOK","decisive_sources":["Galatians 3:10 quoting Deuteronomy 27:26 ('all things which are written in the book of the law') — fixes at least one occurrence to God's whole law, breaking the boundary-marker uniform referent","Romans 3:20 with Romans 3:31 — the law that gives knowledge of sin is established, not abolished, by faith; the denial targets the deeds' claim, not the law","Galatians 2:12-16 — the circumcision-party context supporting the book's contextual assignment of that occurrence","Galatians 3:2, 5 — the constant is receiving the Spirit by faith versus by works of the law, with no disputed act named","Romans 4:4 and Luke 17:10 — the wage/debt mechanism defining the rejected claim","1 Corinthians 7:19 and Acts 16:3 — circumcision is nothing in itself; the error is the demanded purchase price, not the deed","Ephesians 2:9-10 and Titus 3:5, 8 — works excluded as source of the gift, commanded as its fruit"],"unresolved_objections":["The classification of Gal 2:16 as specifically a 'circumcision-party application' rather than simply Torah deeds pressed for justification is plausible from Gal 2:12-14 but not the only viable reading of that occurrence.","The 'purchase price / God in debt' economic framing is explicit in Rom 4:4 but is inferred rather than stated in Gal 3:2, 5 and 3:10; a broader 'means of justification' formulation would fit those texts equally well.","The Rom 9:32 occurrence depends on the TR/KJV text; on the critical text the entry's seven-occurrence list reduces by one, though the book flags this itself.","The 4QMMT parallel is not engaged by the proving chapter and remains the counter's strongest unrebutted external datum, though it bears on background usage rather than Paul's own contextual definitions."],"confidence":"medium"}
